install.title: Install Graupel as an app
install.ios: Tap the Share button (in Safari at the bottom or top of the screen), then choose “Add to Home Screen”.
install.android: Open the browser menu (⋮), then choose “Install app” or “Add to Home screen”.
install.macos: In Safari, choose File › Add to Dock (macOS Sonoma or later).
install.desktop: This browser cannot install Graupel as an app. Open the page in Chrome or Edge and use “Install” in the address bar or the menu.
install.macosOther: This browser cannot install Graupel as an app. Open the page in Safari and choose File › Add to Dock, or use “Install” in Chrome or Edge.
settings.title: Settings
settings.modelChain.text: Shows the weather and the cloud chain as cards above the meteogram; each can be shown or hidden on its own. Hiding a card does not change the forecast: the cloud chain still provides the clouds of the meteogram. Drag the boundaries between the models to shift their time ranges; a newly loaded place starts again with the automatic chain.
settings.startLocation.text: Applies the next time the page opens. “Last selected place” opens the place you viewed last, on the first visit the site's start place. With GPS the page asks for your position when it opens; until it is there, or if it is not allowed, the first favourite is shown.
settings.meteogram.dewPoint.hint: Auto shows the dew point and the spread across the whole chart as soon as the air is nearly saturated (spread up to 5 K) or muggy (dew point from 15 °C) at any time in the period shown and the temperature (2 m) reaches 5 °C at least once in it, otherwise not at all. The dew point is always loaded.
settings.meteogram.scaleToVisibleRange.h: Applies to precipitation and wind: their axes follow the values in the period shown.
settings.archive.days.hint: The installed app keeps every fetch on this device for the history. Fetches older than the chosen number of days are deleted.
settings.archive.historySlider.hint: Shows the days with kept fetches in a bar like the day slider.
settings.transfer.importHint: Loads settings and favourites from a file; the current favourites are replaced.
settings.transfer.error.invalid: This file is not a Graupel settings file. Nothing was changed.
settings.transfer.error.newer: This file comes from a newer version of Graupel and cannot be read. Nothing was changed.
settings.transfer.error.content: This file contains invalid values. Nothing was changed.
settings.note: Settings are saved in this browser only.

menu.label: Menu
history.title: History
info.about.description: Graupel shows meteograms for any place: temperature, wind, precipitation, snow and thunderstorm indicators for the coming days. For each place it joins the weather models of Open-Meteo into a model chain, from high-resolution local models for the first hours to global models for the days after.
info.about.dataModifications: The data were harmonised (units, timestamps) and combined from several weather models into one timeline.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Graupel shows weather forecasts without a user account, without cookies and without tracking. Graupel runs no server of its own and stores no personal data. This page explains which data is nevertheless processed when you visit, by whom and why.
privacy.controller.title: Controller
privacy.controller.text: The controller for this website within the meaning of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is:
privacy.controller.anonymous: This website is run privately and without commercial intent. Details of the operator are given in the imprint.
privacy.hosting.githubPages.title: Hosting on GitHub Pages
privacy.hosting.githubPages.text: The website is served by GitHub Pages, a service of GitHub, Inc., 88 Colin P. Kelly Jr. Street, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA. When you open the page, GitHub processes technically necessary data, in particular your IP address, the date and time of the request and the files requested. According to GitHub, it stores visitors' IP addresses in server logs for security purposes.
privacy.hosting.githubPages.transfer: This involves a transfer of data to the USA. GitHub is certified under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework; for certified companies the European Commission has found an adequate level of data protection (Art. 45 GDPR). GitHub also participates in the UK Extension and in the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework.
privacy.hosting.basis: The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. The legitimate interest is to provide the website reliably and securely.
privacy.hosting.allInkl.title: Hosting at ALL-INKL
privacy.hosting.allInkl.text: The website is hosted by ALL-INKL.COM – Neue Medien Münnich, owner René Münnich, Hauptstraße 68, 02742 Friedersdorf, Germany. When you open the page, ALL-INKL processes technically necessary data, in particular your IP address, the date and time of the request and the files requested, and stores them in server logs.
privacy.hosting.allInkl.retention: According to ALL-INKL, server logs are deleted after seven days at the latest; in individual cases, for example after an attack on its IT systems, they may be kept longer. The servers are located in ALL-INKL's own data centres in Germany; no data is transferred to a country outside the EU.
privacy.weather.title: Weather data from Open-Meteo
privacy.weather.text: Your browser fetches the forecasts directly from Open-Meteo, operated by OpenMeteo GmbH, Hintere Schilligmatte 6, 6463 Bürglen, Switzerland. Open-Meteo receives the coordinates of the chosen place and, for technical reasons, your IP address.
privacy.weather.search: The place search and the elevation of a place are also requested from Open-Meteo. The search term you enter or the coordinates are transmitted for this.
privacy.weather.retention: According to Open-Meteo, it keeps server logs that may contain coordinates and IP addresses and deletes them after 90 days. The European Commission has found that Switzerland provides an adequate level of data protection.
privacy.weather.basis: The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. The legitimate interest is to show the forecast for the place you want; the website cannot work without this request.
privacy.map.title: Map
privacy.map.text: Map tiles are only loaded when you open the map. Your browser then fetches them directly from the map provider, which receives your IP address and the map section shown.
privacy.map.choice: Which of the two following map providers is used depends on your choice in the settings.
privacy.map.opentopomap: The map provider is OpenTopoMap (opentopomap.org), a non-commercial project that creates topographic maps from OpenStreetMap data.
privacy.map.maptoolkit: The map provider is Maptoolkit by Toursprung GmbH, Mariahilfer Straße 93/20, 1060 Vienna, Austria. According to Maptoolkit, it stores only truncated IP addresses and deletes these logs after 15 days at most. The maps are delivered through the Cloudflare network, which may also process requests outside the EU; EU standard contractual clauses apply to this.
privacy.map.basis: The legal basis is Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR. The legitimate interest is to show places on a map.
privacy.location.title: Location and IP address
privacy.location.gps: The website only asks for your location when you press the location button, and only with your browser's permission. The coordinates are only used to request the forecast and the details of this place from Open-Meteo and to load the matching map section from the map provider (OpenTopoMap or Maptoolkit).
privacy.location.ip: Graupel does not determine your location from your IP address. Graupel itself stores neither your location nor your IP address; only the providers named above receive them with each request.
privacy.location.basis: The legal basis for the location request is your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), which you give through the permission in your browser and can withdraw there at any time.
privacy.storage.title: Storage in your browser
privacy.storage.text: The website stores your language, your favourites and your settings in your browser's local storage (localStorage). This data stays on your device and is not transmitted. You can delete it at any time by clearing the site data in your browser.
privacy.storage.noTracking: The website sets no cookies and uses no tracking, analytics or advertising services.
privacy.storage.basis: This storage is strictly necessary for the functions you request (Art. 5(3) of the ePrivacy Directive).
privacy.rights.title: Your rights
privacy.rights.text: Under the GDPR you have the right of access (Art. 15), rectification (Art. 16), erasure (Art. 17), restriction of processing (Art. 18) and data portability (Art. 20), and the right to object to processing based on Art. 6(1)(f) (Art. 21). You can withdraw consent at any time with effect for the future (Art. 7(3)).
privacy.rights.note: As Graupel itself stores no personal data, data in server logs is held only by the providers named above. You can also exercise your rights directly with them.
privacy.rights.complaint: You also have the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority (Art. 77 GDPR), in particular in the Member State of your habitual residence, place of work or place of the alleged infringement.
privacy.switzerland.title: Note for Switzerland
privacy.switzerland.text: For visitors from Switzerland, the Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP, revised since 1 September 2023) also applies. The processing described and your rights apply accordingly.
privacy.switzerland.githubPages: The transfer to GitHub in the USA is based on the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, which the Federal Council has recognised as adequate since 15 September 2024.
privacy.switzerland.allInkl: The website is hosted by ALL-INKL in Germany, a country whose data protection the Federal Council recognises as adequate (Annex 1 of the Data Protection Ordinance, DPO).
privacy.switzerland.complaint: You can report concerns to the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (FDPIC).

modelChain.horizon.intro: Max (from now) {available} h / {catalogue} h: the model’s longest run is {catalogue} h long (catalogue horizon); from the current hour on, the data reaches {available} h.
modelChain.horizon.full: The data reaches the full catalogue horizon from now.
modelChain.horizon.mixed: Open-Meteo keeps one continuous series per model: a new run only overwrites the hours it computes. The latest run ({run}) is shorter than what earlier runs still have, so it only covers until {end} ({hours} h from now).
modelChain.horizon.earlier: The earlier run {run} reaches further, so its hours from {from} until {until} complete the picture.
modelChain.horizon.together: Together they deliver {available} h from now ({now}).
modelChain.horizon.limited: The latest run started {run} and is {length} h long; it started {age} h before the current hour ({now}), so its data ends {end}: only {available} h are left from now.
modelChain.horizon.limitedNoLength: The latest run started {run}, {age} h before the current hour ({now}), so its data ends {end}: only {available} h are left from now.
modelChain.horizon.limitedNoRun: The latest run started before the current hour, so only {available} h of it are left from now.
